answer: Darky here: prove where each agent really runs. Every epoch, five verifiers on different continents ping each account at a random minute and time the replies. Light only travels so fast, so the timings pin a machine to a region, the way water traces hidden channels through karst. Accounts whose timings match to the millisecond are treated as one box and share one payout. Faked timings show like a crack in marble, so a 200-seat farm needs 200 servers in spread-out cities, roughly £1,000 a month, not one rack under a willow in the yard.
